rationale: Large multi-center cohort analysis demonstrates that bi-allelic pathogenic variants in ACBD6 (predominantly loss-of-function, 18/20 distinct variants) cause neurodevelopmental disorder with progressive movement abnormalities (OMIM #620785). Global developmental delay and intellectual disability are observed in 100% (45/45) of reported individuals. Progressive movement disorders are present in 97% (43/45), with dystonia being the most prevalent movement disorder manifestation (94%, 42/45), frequently accompanied by hyperkinetic movements including chorea, tremor, ataxia, and subsequent parkinsonism/hypokinesia.

evidence.text: In a seminal cohort of 45 affected individuals across 28 unrelated families with bi-allelic pathogenic ACBD6 variants, 100% presented with moderate-to-severe global developmental delay/intellectual disability, 97% had movement disorders (with dystonia present in 94%), 98% had expressive language impairment, 97% developed progressive postural deformities, 85% had cerebellar ataxia, and 76% exhibited spasticity/hypertonia.

source.title: Bi-allelic ACBD6 variants lead to a neurodevelopmental syndrome with progressive and complex movement disorders
source.quote: The affected individuals (23 males and 22 females), aged 1-50 years, typically present with a complex and progressive disease involving moderate-to-severe global developmental delay/intellectual disability (100%) with significant expressive language impairment (98%), movement disorders (97%), facial dysmorphism (95%) and mild cerebellar ataxia (85%) associated with gait impairment (94%), limb spasticity/hypertonia (76%)... The most conspicuous and common movement disorder was dystonia (94%), frequently leading to early-onset progressive postural deformities (97%), limb dystonia (55%) and cervical dystonia (31%).

evidence.text: Review of genetic causes of chorea and hyperkinetic disorders identifies bi-allelic loss-of-function variants in ACBD6 as a novel cause of hyperkinetic syndromes presenting with chorea, dystonia, and parkinsonism.

source.title: Update on Genetic Chorea
source.quote: Several novel genetic conditions have been linked to chorea over the last 3 years, including mutations in FTH1, NAA60, ACBD6 or TOR1AIP2.

evidence.text: Comprehensive analysis of monogenic neurodevelopmental disorders and developmental epileptic encephalopathies presenting with hyperkinetic movement disorders highlights that recessive ACBD6 mutations present prominently with axial dystonia as a distinguishing sign within hyperkinetic NDDs.

new_directions.question_text: How specifically can neuroimaging hallmarks (corpus callosum anomalies, clava hypertrophy, and anterior commissure agenesis) differentiate ACBD6-related disorders from other hereditary dystonia-parkinsonism and chorea syndromes?
new_directions.rationale: Neuroimaging abnormalities such as hypoplasia/agenesis of the anterior commissure (66%) and hypertrophy of the clava (24%) may provide pathognomonic diagnostic clues in individuals with ambiguous mixed hyperkinetic/dystonic phenotypes.

new_directions.question_text: What is the therapeutic responsiveness of ACBD6-associated dystonia, chorea, and tremor to dopaminergic modulation, anticholinergics, or deep brain stimulation?
new_directions.rationale: Patients present with a progression from hyperkinetic/dystonic features in childhood to parkinsonism in older ages (32%), suggesting possible basal ganglia dopaminergic pathway involvement.
